ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: France applies the Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Articles L.561-1 et seq. and R.561-3-1 et seq.; the French Commercial Code Articles L.123-4-2 and R.123-4-3 et seq. concerning the beneficial owners register; Décret n° 2016-252 du 1er mars 2016 implementing the beneficial owners declaration; and the European AML/CFT framework under Directive 2015/849/EU as amended by Directive 2018/843/EU. For discretionary trust administration, the French beneficial ownership disclosure also captures settlors, protectors, beneficiaries, and other natural persons exercising effective control over trust assets to the extent required by CMF Article L.561-2-2 and the Code général des impôts reporting regime for foreign trusts.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, trust protectors and beneficiaries against the French Administrative Freezing lists (FRO), the European Union consolidated sanctions lists under Regulation 269/2014 and 833/2014 as amended, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, and OFAC SDN and NS-MA lists for USD-denominated transfers. Politically exposed persons are treated as higher-risk clients under CMF Articles L.561-10 and R.561-19, requiring senior management approval, enhanced ongoing monitoring, source-of-wealth documentation and immediate reporting to Tracfin of any unusual, suspicious or refused transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI - Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; ancillary national company name search through the Infogreffe RCS database
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the official legal language. The company name must be written in Latin characters and may include foreign words only where a French transliteration or translation is provided in the incorporation filings. The name must be distinctive, lawful, non-deceptive and must not create confusion with an existing French or EU protected corporate name or trademark. The suffix 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' or the short form 'SAS' must be appended to the corporate name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a final name rejection issued by the Guichet unique or the RCS registrar, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal within two months of the notice. The appeal must be addressed to the registrar of the competent tribunal de commerce and must attach the original rejection decision, corrected proposed name, and any prior ministerial or ACPR authorization required for sensitive tokens. If the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may initiate a judicial action before the commercial court under the French procedural rules applicable to registrations (procédure gracieuse) seeking annulment of the refusal and compulsory registration; representation by a French bar-admitted lawyer is mandatory.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Administrative domiciliation by a registered domiciliation company is expressly permitted for a French SAS under Article L.123-11-1 of the French Commercial Code and may satisfy the initial registration address. For a high-risk discretionary trust administration business under ISIC 6430, a purely virtual office is not acceptable as a final operational substance model. French regulators and the licensing authority expect a genuine establishment in France, including a fixed office, qualified local management, physical or securely accessible records, a resident compliance officer, and documented management autonomy in respect of the trust assets for which the company acts as fiduciary administrator.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated annual probability, estimated at 35%, rising to approximately 55% within the first two years of operation under the special high-risk trust licence. The quantification reflects the mandatory licensing, the client acceptance file burden, and the enhanced supervisory and Tracfin reporting obligations imposed on French fiduciaries and trust administrators.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - Official portal: https://www.impots.gouv.fr/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French-resident entities (including SAS) are automatically assigned a SIREN/SIRET tax identification number upon incorporation and registration with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS). Foreign entities seeking to establish operations in France must register with the DGFiP to procure a French TIN and VAT identification number (FR followed by SIREN).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box elections available in France. However, hybrid mismatch rules under the Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) apply, and certain entities may opt into specific tax regimes such as the micro-entreprise or EI regimes, though SAS typically defaults to standard corporate taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €77,700 annual turnover threshold for services (previous year); €33,300 for goods
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing for B2B transactions under French law (effective 2024), requiring API integration with the DGFiP's fiscal clearance platform and issuance of digital fiscal stamps (estampille fiscale) for compliant invoicing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods outside the EU with proof of actual export; for offshore services provided to non-EU clients, zero-rating if the service is not performed in France and client is non-resident. For fiduciary trust administration, eligibility requires documentation establishing the offshore nature and non-performance in France.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent claims of zero-rating result in repayment of the VAT amount plus penalties up to 80% of the evaded tax, interest charges, and potential criminal prosecution under French tax law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank; foreign-exchange and customs reporting may also involve the French Ministry for the Economy and Finance, the Directorate-General of Customs and Indirect Taxes (DGDDI), and the Directorate-General of the Treasury.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a euro-area jurisdiction with full current-account convertibility and no general exchange-control approval for ordinary commercial payments, dividend distributions, interest payments, service fees, or capital repatriation. Capital movements are generally liberalized under European Union law and French monetary and financial law. Banks may require evidence of the legal basis, beneficial ownership, source and destination of funds, tax compliance, underlying contracts, and corporate approvals. Outbound distributions remain subject to French corporate-law solvency and distributable-profit rules, withholding-tax analysis, transfer-pricing requirements, anti-abuse provisions, beneficial-ownership verification, and applicable treaty or European Union relief conditions. A French SAS administering irrevocable offshore asset-protection trusts presents elevated scrutiny because trustees, settlors, protectors, beneficiaries, and controlling persons may create complex beneficial-ownership and tax-transparency issues. The proposed activity must not involve unauthorized payment services, deposit-taking, portfolio management, fiduciary activities reserved to regulated professionals, concealment of assets, evasion of French trust reporting, or circumvention of sanctions and anti-money-laundering controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the central bank and no mandatory conversion ratio or universal repatriation deadline for export receipts. Export proceeds may generally remain in euros or foreign currency, subject to the contractual banking arrangements and ordinary accounting, tax, customs, and anti-money-laundering controls. The company must retain commercial invoices, customs evidence, transport documentation, payment records, and proof of the underlying transaction. Foreign-currency balances and transactions must be recorded and translated in accordance with French accounting rules. Banks may require transaction-purpose information and may apply internal monitoring or reporting procedures. Sector-specific rules, sanctions restrictions, cash-reporting requirements, and statistical reporting obligations can apply. No export-receipt rule should be treated as permitting the company to hold or move client trust assets through its own operating account.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; segregated client or fiduciary account only if legally justified, contractually documented, and accepted under the bank's regulated-activity and safeguarding framework
Operational Account; potential dedicated client-funds account subject to legal qualification, enhanced due diligence, and bank approval

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank and relevant Crédit Agricole group entity
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; capital or escrow account where required for a specific corporate transaction; client-money arrangements subject to regulated-activity review

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque Populaire Rives de Paris or another relevant BPCE group commercial bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; transaction-specific escrow or segregated account only after legal and compliance approval
Operational Account; limited suitability for high-risk cross-border fiduciary structures and subject to enhanced onboarding

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium for ordinary corporate treasury and Low for discretionary offshore trust administration. An offshore digital electronic-money institution cannot be assumed to provide lawful French deposit-taking, payment services, safeguarding, fiduciary custody, or client-money services. The provider must be authorized under the applicable European Union regime, passported or otherwise permitted to serve France, and capable of supporting the relevant currencies, sanctions screening, safeguarding model, account nomenclature, and regulatory reporting. An EMI account is not a bank deposit and generally cannot replace a regulated client-money, escrow, trust, or custody account. Use of an offshore EMI may trigger enhanced scrutiny, transaction delays, account closure, and inability to evidence segregation of trust assets. Payment initiation, money remittance, account information, custody, investment, or asset-management functions may require separate authorization. The SAS should use a regulated French or European banking institution for core operating, capital, and any legally required segregated accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal rule that every director must appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the bank accepts qualified electronic identification, documentary verification, video identification, and reliable electronic signatures. In practice, banks commonly require interviews with the legal representative, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, and relevant compliance officers. Physical attendance, notarized or apostilled documents, certified translations, wet-ink signatures, or an in-person meeting may be required for a high-risk offshore trust business, non-resident ownership, complex ownership chains, foreign trustees, politically exposed persons, adverse media, unexplained source of wealth, or requests for segregated client accounts. The bank's internal risk policy controls the final requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business activity described as discretionary asset-protection trust administration, spendthrift trust management, or offshore trust structuring without a clearly defined legal and regulatory perimeter
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; legal memorandum identifying every regulated and unregulated activity; service-flow diagram; list of jurisdictions and counterparties; confirmation of whether the company will ever receive, control, invest, transmit, or safeguard client assets; applicable professional registrations or authorizations; independent compliance manual; and board-approved prohibition on unauthorized financial, payment, custody, or investment activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership involving settlors, protectors, trustees, beneficiaries, nominees, private foundations, or layered offshore entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate structure chart; constitutional documents; registers of shareholders and directors; certified identification and address evidence for all direct and indirect owners and controllers; trust deeds and amendments; letters of wishes where relevant; protector powers; beneficiary classes; trustee details; control analysis; and French trust-register and tax-reporting assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Client funds proposed to be held in the SAS's ordinary operating account or commingled with corporate funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Funds-flow policy; account segregation map; proposed account titles; trust or escrow agreements; accounting controls; reconciliation procedures; authorized-signatory matrix; independent review arrangements; evidence of any required payment, custody, investment, legal, or fiduciary authorization; and written bank confirmation that the proposed account structure is permitted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth or source of funds inconsistent with asset-protection, inheritance, private-equity, crypto, real-estate, or offshore explanations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax returns; audited financial statements; sale agreements; inheritance or probate records; employment and business-income evidence; bank statements; loan agreements; investment statements; notarized declarations; documentary chain of funds; tax-residence certificates; and sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media screening results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential French tax evasion, concealment of assets, sham transactions, fraudulent insolvency, or improper transfer of assets to defeat creditors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent French legal opinion; solvency and creditor-rights analysis; transaction-purpose memorandum; tax advice covering trust disclosure and taxation; evidence of arm's-length consideration; client acceptance criteria; refusal and escalation procedures; no-assistance clause for evasion or asset concealment; and documented beneficial-owner tax compliance confirmations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned persons, sanctioned sectors, dual-use goods, or payments involving restricted counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-risk matrix; sanctions-screening methodology; screening records for all relevant parties and vessels; transaction monitoring rules; export-control analysis; payment approval workflow; escalation logs; and documented refusal or blocking procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal, nominee, virtual-office, mailbox, or residential addresses that do not evidence genuine French economic activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or ownership evidence for the registered office; operating-site evidence; payroll and management records; French tax registrations; utility or occupancy evidence; customer and supplier contracts; board-meeting records; local director and employee roles; and explanation of the company's actual management and control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection, unexplained shareholder loan, circular funding, or capital from an unrelated third party
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription or loan agreement; corporate approvals; bank-origin evidence; audited source-of-funds trail; ultimate beneficial-owner confirmation; valuation support; capital-accounting documentation; foreign-investment reporting assessment; and evidence that the transfer is not client money or a disguised deposit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border payments that do not match the stated trust-administration revenue model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Expected transaction profile; client and counterparty register; sample contracts and invoices; payment-purpose taxonomy; monthly transaction forecasts; reconciliation reports; dual approval controls; sanctions and AML monitoring configuration; and management information reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reliance on an offshore EMI, virtual IBAN, cryptoasset platform, or unregulated custodian for client or trust assets
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provider authorization and passporting evidence; safeguarding or custody terms; legal opinion on territorial scope; account ownership and beneficiary analysis; segregation evidence; audit reports; regulatory status checks; counterparty due diligence; and board approval with fallback banking arrangements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder equity through a French or European regulated bank into the SAS corporate account or a transaction-specific capital account, using SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments and SWIFT cross-border payment messaging for non-SEPA currencies. The remittance package should include the subscription agreement, shareholder or board resolutions, capital increase documentation, bank-origin evidence, ultimate-beneficial-owner data, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence, tax-residence information, and the correct payment narrative. The receiving bank should confirm whether any Banque de France statistical reporting, foreign-direct-investment reporting, or other regulatory filing is required; reporting thresholds and classifications must be assessed transaction by transaction. Shareholder loans require a written agreement, arm's-length terms, transfer-pricing analysis, withholding-tax review, and accounting treatment. Do not route trust or beneficiary assets as paid-in capital, shareholder loans, revenue, or intercompany funds. For non-euro transfers, retain the SWIFT payment reference, exchange-rate evidence, correspondent-bank details, and reconciliation documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer where available for euro payments to eligible beneficiaries. Use SWIFT customer payments, including MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent, for non-SEPA payments, with complete ordering-customer, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice, and payment-purpose information. Use commercial documentary letters of credit, including an irrevocable letter of credit subject to UCP 600, for higher-risk goods or counterparties where documentary control is commercially justified. Documentary collections under URC 522 may be used where appropriate. Match every payment to an approved contract, invoice, customs or shipping record, and verified beneficiary account. Apply sanctions, export-control, dual-use, anti-bribery, and transaction-monitoring screening before release. Client trust assets and beneficiary distributions must be paid only from an appropriately segregated account and only under documented trust, court, contractual, tax, and corporate authority. Banks may reject or delay payments that lack transparent purpose, beneficial-owner information, or evidence of underlying activity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards for documented commercial exposures, subject to bank suitability, appropriateness, collateral, confirmation, accounting, and risk-limit procedures.
Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity management and currency conversion, provided they are used for genuine treasury needs and documented under the bank's master agreement.
Currency options or collars for defined operating, trade, or financing exposures, subject to treasury policy, valuation controls, premium funding, suitability review, and board-approved limits.

Non-deliverable forwards only for currencies or markets where settlement through a regulated bank is legally available and the instrument is used for a genuine hedging exposure; French and European market-abuse, EMIR, reporting, collateral, and counterparty requirements may apply.

Cross-currency swaps for documented financing or long-term currency exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, counterparty credit limits, collateral terms, valuation, hedge-accounting analysis, and EMIR compliance where applicable.

No speculative derivatives trading, leveraged retail-style products, or hedging of unidentified client or trust assets should be permitted. A written treasury policy should define eligible exposures, counterparties, approval thresholds, segregation of duties, valuation methodology, collateral management, hedge effectiveness, and independent reconciliation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders for approval; Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du tribunal de commerce) for filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approve accounts within six months after fiscal year-end; file within one month after approval, or two months for electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a court injunction and periodic penalty payments; failure to comply with an injunction may result in a civil fine. No fixed automatic strike-off period applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end, or by the second working day after 1 May for a calendar-year taxpayer, subject to the applicable electronic-filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally triggers a 10% surcharge, increased in specified circumstances, plus late-payment interest; tax reassessment and collection measures may follow.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner information update, if reportable information has changed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du tribunal de commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File within 30 days after a change to reportable beneficial-owner information; no routine annual confirmation is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or inaccurate information may result in criminal penalties, including fines and, in serious cases, imprisonment; the court may order compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally required when the SAS exceeds at least two of these thresholds at its financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, or 50 employees. Group-specific rules and other statutory triggers may also require an auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French General Accounting Plan (Plan comptable général); IFRS applies to consolidated accounts where required or elected under applicable law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation is required. Reportable changes must generally be filed with the Commercial Court Registry within 30 days. Maintain current corporate records and document share transfers and corporate decisions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes and written decisions of shareholders and corporate officers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000-15,000 per year, depending on complexity and scope

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 25% standard rate; reduced rate of 15% for SMEs meeting turnover and employee thresholds; R&D tax credit up to 30% of eligible expenditures; accelerated depreciation and investment tax credit available

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 1200-A (Déclaration de résultat des sociétés) filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after fiscal year-end (April 30 for calendar-year fiscal year ending 31 December)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-source income for non-resident entities with French branch or permanent establishment
Adjust for non-deductible expenses, add back non-taxable income, and apply transfer pricing adjustments
Apply 25% rate to taxable profit; claim any applicable tax credits or reduced rates
Withholding tax may apply to non-resident recipients; report gross and net amounts

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 0.5% of tax due per month of delay (maximum 5%); daily interest of 0.2% on unpaid tax; criminal penalties including fines up to 80% of evaded tax and imprisonment for willful evasion

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from French tax authorities; submit TRC together with DTA application via impots.gouv.fr portal or competent authority; reduce WHT to treaty rate upon approval (typically 2-4 weeks processing time)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% to 15% under DTAs (statutory rate 25% without treaty); interest: 0% to 15% under DTAs (statutory rate 25% without treaty); related-party interest subject to arm's length documentation

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million annual turnover threshold triggers mandatory Local File and Master File documentation
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France implements EU Economic Substance Directive; ESR applies to holding, IP holding, finance, and certain service entities; requires adequate substance in France including qualified employees, core income-generating activities, and physical presence

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or understatement of taxable income through false invoices, fictitious expenses, or non-disclosure of related-party transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to 80% of evaded tax, imprisonment up to 5 years, and full restitution of unpaid taxes plus interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability, fines, and possible imprisonment; corporate veil may be pierced leading to personal restitution obligations

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SAS as a nominal entity without economic substance or using it for artificial profit shifting or treaty shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of transactions, denial of all tax benefits, penalties up to 500% of tax advantage obtained, and potential criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for damages and possible disqualification from management positions
